layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The effects of nitrogen alloying on pitting corrosion of type 316LN and 20 wt.% Mn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: substituted type 316LN stainless steels were investigated by potentiodynamic polarization tests

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Cl⁻ ion-bearing neutral and acidic solutions. Pitting resistance was markedly improved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through the nitrogen alloying in both types of alloys, compared with the nitrogen-free alloys. It

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was confirmed that the added nitrogen was solid-solutioned in the austenitic phase without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forming any nitrides under 20 min heat treatment at 1150°C. From the in situ observation on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the initiation and growth of pits, pitting was found to occur consistently at the sites of inclu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sions. The pitting corrosion behaviors in both types of alloys were discussed with respect to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: role of sulfides as initiators of pitting corrosion, and the changes of repassivation properties due

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the nitrogen alloying in the alloys. © 2000 Published by Elsevier Science Ltd.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The beneficial effects of nitrogen, as an alloying element, to the mechanical and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion properties of many austenitic stainless steels (SS) have been well recognized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: over the last two decades. In particular, it has been reported that nitrogen alloying can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lead to improvements in pitting resistance of the alloys in Cl- ion-bearing neutral and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acidic solutions [1,2]. In SS, however, the beneficial effects of nitrogen are limited by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the maximum solubility of nitrogen in solid solution. For example, the nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solubility in Fe–17Cr–14Ni SS is only about 0.17 wt.% at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under 1 atm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gas

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pressure [3]. Precipitation of nitrides, such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , due to the excess nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: above the solubility limit) may lead to a localized depletion of Cr and hence induce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localized corrosion around them.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The influence of Mn, a common alloying element in SS, on the resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion of SS is not clearly elucidated as yet. Some studies performed on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cr-Ni–Mn–Mo alloys containing up to 10 wt.% Mn found improved pitting re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sistance in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution tests [4]. However, a contradictory result with Mn al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loying was also reported [5]. The presence of MnS inclusions, formed due to Mn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloyed with SS and S present as an impurity, increases the susceptibility of SS to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion. Hence, the AISI ¹ 300 series standard grade specifies the maximum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mn and S contents of 2 and 0.03 wt.%, respectively. However, Mn has a strong

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: affinity to nitrogen and thus increases the solubility of nitrogen substantially [6,7]. At

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low contents, Mn is regarded as an austenite former [8], whereas at higher contents it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is thought to favor ferrite [8,9].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The nucleation sites of pits are usually found to be associated with inclusions on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SS. In particular, sulfide inclusions such as MnS and FeS were shown to be the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential sites in the extensive works of Wraglen [10], Eklund [11], and others [12–

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 14]. They have all clearly shown that the dissolution of a sulfide inclusion is the initial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: step of pit propagation at this site in Cl- ion-bearing neutral and acidic solutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Therefore, it is useful to combine the electrochemical and metallographic studies to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully understand the pitting corrosion behaviors of the alloys.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the present work, the effects of the nitrogen alloying on the pitting corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties of type 316LN and 20 wt.% Mn-substituted type 316LN SS in neutral and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acidic Cl- media were studied using potentiodynamic polarization tests. Since the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: microstructure including second phases of the alloy strongly affects the pitting cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rosion behavior, they were investigated using microscopic equipment. The in situ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: monitoring of pitting was also carried out using an optical microscope to identify the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting initiation sites and to understand the pitting growth features. Finally, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: difference in pitting corrosion resistance between the two types of alloys was com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pared and discussed considering the microstructures, the inclusions involved, and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: repassivation properties of the alloys.

layout_dets.text: 2. Experimental method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1. Materials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Two types of model alloys, type 316LN SS and 20 wt.% Mn-substituted type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 316LN SS, were obtained from the National Research Institute for Metals (NRIM),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Japan, and the chemical compositions are shown in Table 1. The alloys were in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duction melted in a vacuum furnace and cast into ingots. The ingots were hot-rolled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in a controlled atmosphere, and then cold-rolled to 2.154 mm thick sheets. Before the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experiments, all specimens were solution annealed for 20 min at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: water quenched. For type 316LN SS under consideration (L series in Table 1), ni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trogen is the only major compositional variable because Cr, Ni and Mo are essen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tially constant and the carbon contents are extremely low. Similarly, for the high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mn-substituted type 316LN SS (M series in Table 1), 20 wt.% Fe was substituted for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 20 wt.% Mn to increase the nitrogen solubility.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2. Potentiodynamic polarization tests

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cu-wire was spot-welded to one side of each specimen, mounted in epoxy resin,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and ground to 2000 grade silicon carbide. To avoid crevice corrosion, the specimen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mount interface was carefully coated with a thin film of silicone sealant. Approxi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mately 1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the surface was exposed to the test solution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All the solutions were prepared from double-distilled water and the chemicals

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were analytical-grade reagents. Several test solutions, 1, 0.1 M KCl, and 0.5 M HCl,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were chosen for the investigation. The test solutions were degassed by purging the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions with purified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gas before and during each potentiodynamic polarization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Potentiodynamic polarization tests were performed using a three-electrode cell

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system consisting of a saturated calomel electrode (SCE) as a reference, a platinum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrode as a counter, and a specimen as the working electrode. The sample was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: kept immersed in the test solution for 2 h at open-circuit potential. After obtaining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the stable corrosion potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , the potential was raised in the anodic direction,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from –100 mV below

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , at a scan rate of 0.2 mV/s. All the potentials were referred

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to an SCE. The potentiodynamic polarization tests in different solutions were carried

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: out at room temperature, and repeated at least twice for each specimen to ensure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reproducibility. The presence of pitting was confirmed by an optical microscope after

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the corrosion tests.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 2.4. In situ observation of the pitting process

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To obtain information on the sites of pit initiation and growing features of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stable pits in the alloys, an in situ experiment of the pitting process was performed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using a scanning probe microscope (SPM; Model SPA300, Seiko Instruments Inc.).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The SPM was originally designed to study surface properties of materials such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surface morphology and electrostatic potential distribution. It is also possible to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conduct electrochemical tests using an electrochemical cell and an electrochemical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: controller contained within the SPM, and to view the corrosion process using an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optical microscope positioned over the electrochemical cell.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A test solution of 0.1 M KCl was chosen with air-saturation at room temperature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the investigation. The specimen with a size of approximately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanically polished with diamond paste to a size of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . The specimen, except

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the test area of approximately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , was painted carefully with a corrosion-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistant enamel to avoid crevice corrosion between the specimen surface and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: O-ring of the electrochemical cell. The potential was raised anodically from —500 mV,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is far below

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the alloys, at a scan rate of 0.2 mV/s. As soon as the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was initiated in the test area, the applied potential was switched off so that the stable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pit(s) could grow in an autocatalytic manner.

layout_dets.text: 3. Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1. Potentiodynamic polarization tests

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The potentiodynamic responses of the L series in 1 M KCl solution are shown in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1(a). As reported [1,2,15], the resistance to pitting corrosion of the L series,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluated by the pitting potential, increased with increasing nitrogen content in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys. The M series, however, showed a very complicated behavior. The resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to pitting corrosion of the M series was very inferior to those of the L series in 1 M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: KCl solution. Further, the M series exhibited numerous current transients in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anodic polarization regions below the pitting potentials, as shown in Fig. 1(b).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To further study the current transients that appeared in the anodic polarization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the M series, the anodic polarization behaviors of the M series were examined in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the less concentrated solution of 0.1 M KCl. Current-potential traces in the passive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range of the M series are presented in Fig. 2. Evidently, nitrogen effects on the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with increasing nitrogen content. However, the behavior was more complicated for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the M series. The results showed that the pitting resistance of the M series is quite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The first finding of the present work is that pitting was initiated almost exclusively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at non-metallic inclusions, probably MnS. Secondly, high Mn alloying (20 wt.%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the present case) was detrimental to pitting corrosion of type 316LN SS, even

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: though the nitrogen solubility could be significantly raised. Lastly, the beneficial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects of the nitrogen alloying on the resistance to pitting corrosion, when nitrogen is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solid-solutioned in the austenitic phase, were confirmed in the M series, as well as in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the L series.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Y.S. Lim et al. / Corrosion Science 43 (2001) 53–68

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Eklund [11] pointed out that the sulfides are electronic conductors, and can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: therefore be polarized to the potential of a passive SS surface (i.e., to the open-circuit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential) in natural corrosive environments. At this potential, from the results of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thermodynamic considerations, the sulfides themselves are not thermodynami-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cally stable and tend to dissolve making a microcrevice at the periphery along

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the inclusion/metal interface. If there are Cl⁻ ions in the solution, the Cl- ions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are preferentially adsorbed on the polarized surface of MnS, due to the high elec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tronic conductivity of MnS [10], which should further facilitate its anodic dissolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Most of the MnS inclusions found in the M series, in the present study, were large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and had an elongated-shape. Stewart and Williams [12] have investigated anodic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: current transients in neutral dilute NaCl solutions (0.028 M) for laser-treated type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 304L SS with various sulfur contents. Laser surface melting (LSM) was shown to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: markedly improve the pitting resistance of the alloys, due to the refinement of size as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as the reduction of the (visible) volume fraction of sulfur-rich inclusions. They

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: showed that the bulk sulfur content of an alloy does not in itself control pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: susceptibility, rather it is the size, shape and distribution of the sulfide inclusions that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is significant. They concluded that sulfide inclusions below a certain critical size did

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not act as initiation sites for damaging pits. The above results can be interpreted as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indicating that the Cl⁻ ion concentration within the pit attracted by anodic dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution of the small inclusions never reaches the critical concentration for the pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cipitation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: salt films, and consequently repassivation of the metastable pit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occurs. It is known that salt film precipitation is the precursor of pitting, and salt film

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formation is therefore important in stabilizing pit growth in SS [17,18]. Therefore,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the surface layer resistant to pitting corrosion formed by LSM can provide an ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fective barrier between the corrosive environment and the underlying pitting sus-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ceptible alloy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The early stage of pitting initiation could be understood by the current transients

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occurred in the passive potential regime (Fig. 2). As the pits developed at the sites of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sulfide inclusions, the current transients should be closely correlated with the be-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: havior of the passive film around them. The absence of current transients on the L

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: series under the same conditions can be partly attributed to the sparseness or absence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the sulfide inclusions as a pitting source, and consequently relative high pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentials. Once a pit embryo nucleates, it could grow steadily at the high applied

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential in L series, as pointed out by Palit et al. [1].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For a variety of SS in dilute Cl- solution, Williams et al. [19–21] showed that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frequency of propagating pits is proportional to the frequency of nucleation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metastable pits (or the frequency of current transients in the polarization test), and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that the survival probability of a metastable pit drops drastically to zero as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applied potential (nominally, pitting potential in the polarization test) approaches a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: certain value. This explains why the M series is more susceptible to pitting corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than the L series. The number density of sulfide inclusions in the M series was much

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher than that in the L series. Obviously, the passive film could be altered by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mn alloying, affecting the resistance to pitting corrosion. The precise effects have not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yet been reported.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Y.S. Lim et al. / Corrosion Science 43 (2001) 53–68

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Whether the metastable pit becomes stable and continuously grows, is dependent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the ability of the SS to repassivate the exposed base metal around the dissolving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MnS inclusion. To understand the effects of N alloying on the resistance to pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion, it is necessary to know at what point repassivation of the exposed base

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal within a pit should cease, and which factors affect the criteria for stable pit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: growth. The development of the pit embryo into a growing pit can be envisaged from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model for pit initiation at MnS proposed by Baker and Castle [14]. As MnS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dissolves, the base metal is exposed to the corrosive environment, making a crevice-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like cavity between the exposed base metal and MnS. Depending on the Cl- ion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentration, pH and applied potential, the repassivation of the exposed part of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: base metal within the pit will occur. If the volume and size of the MnS inclusion are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small [12] such that the concentration of Cl⁻ ions does not exceed the critical value

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for precipitation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: salt film, the exposed base metal will repassivate and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pit will cease growing. If, however, salt film saturation is attained within the cavity,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: salt film will form at the surface of the exposed base metal, and lead to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: continuously growing pit by preventing the repassivation reaction. In the present

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study, the effects of nitrogen alloying on SS were realized as causing reductions in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frequency of the current transients and in the height of the individual current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transient in the passive potential regime, and the resultant increase of the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentials. As Jargelius-Pettersson [2] claimed, the observation strongly suggests that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen promoted pit repassivation, i.e., in this case, easier formation of the passive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: film within the pit during MnS dissolution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The cathodic dissolution of N for NH† production [22] is too sluggish at high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applied potentials in the L series [23], and the amount of acid consumption by NH‡

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: production is rather marginal, as shown by Newman and Shahrabi [24]. The sites of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initiation of pitting were not the base metal itself, but the sulfide inclusions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Therefore, the beneficial effects due to nitrogen dissolution might not be operative in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the early stage of initiation of pitting in the present study.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Pitting was initiated almost exclusively at non-metallic inclusions in both types of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys, in particular, MnS in 20 wt.% Mn-substituted SS. The volume, size and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shape of the sulfides present in the alloys provided the suitable conditions for a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pit embryo to evolve into a steadily growing pit under the present experimental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Nitrogen alloying had markedly beneficial effects on the resistance to pitting cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rosion of the alloys in the solutions under investigation. High Mn alloying in type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 316LN SS was detrimental to pitting corrosion, even though higher levels of nitro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gen could be obtained.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. The nitrogen effect was realized by the pronounced increase of the pitting poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tials in both types of alloys. In addition, the current transients due to metastable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pits in the passive potential regime were significantly suppressed by nitrogen alloy-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing in 20 wt.% Mn-substituted type 316LN SS. From these results, it is believed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Y.S. Lim et al. / Corrosion Science 43 (2001) 53–68

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that nitrogen alloyed to SS could facilitate the repassivation process of the ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posed base metal within the pit during MnS dissolution.
